pairs.question: Binas aedes habeo, alteras tibi lego, heres aedes alteras altius tollit et luminibus tuis officit: quid cum illo agere potes? et an interesse putes, suas aedes altius tollat an hereditarias? et de illo quaero, an per alienas aedes accessum heres ad eam rem quae legatur praestare debet, sicut solet quaeri, cum usus fructus loci legatus est, ad quem locum accedi nisi per alienum non potest.
pairs.answer: Qui binas aedes habebat, si alteras legavit, non dubium est, quin heres alias possit altius tollendo obscurare lumina legatarum aedium.
pairs.derivation: Gaurus's entire letter to Marcellus is one extended question (it poses three interrogatives: quid cum illo agere potes?, an interesse putes...?, an... praestare debet?). Quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question; the framing tag 'Gaurus Marcello:' was dropped. The reply tag 'Marcellus respondit:' was dropped and the answer cut at the first full stop (after 'legatarum aedium'); what follows is elaboration ('idem dicendum est, si...').

pairs.question: An olympicus aditum praestare deberet?
pairs.answer: Servitutem quidem non esse, sed heredem transire per domum ad ea quae commemorata sunt posse, dum non noceat legatario.
pairs.derivation: Setup ('Olympico habitationem et horreum... aditus fuit') establishes the referents but the operative interrogative is 'an olympicus aditum praestare deberet'; the framing 'quaesitum est' was dropped. Answer follows 'respondi' (dropped); kept whole as the single sentence that actually answers.

pairs.question: Cum neque luminibus publii maevii vicini neque itineri vicini officeret neque stillicidium ne vicini domo cadat, an aliquam actionem publius maevius vicinus ad prohibendum haberet?
pairs.answer: Secundum ea quae proponerentur nullam habere.
pairs.derivation: Framing 'quaero' was dropped; the conditional clauses are part of the speaker's own interrogative and are kept for the referent of 'aliquam actionem'. Answer follows 'respondi' (dropped); the single answering clause kept verbatim.

pairs.question: Qui duo praedia confinia habuerat, superiorem fundum vendiderat: in lege ita dixerat, ut aquam sulco aperto emptori educere in fundum inferiorem recte liceat: si emptor ex alio fundo aquam acciperet et eam in inferiorem ducere vellet, an possit id suo iure facere nec ne?
pairs.answer: Nihil amplius, quam quod ipsius fundi siccandi causa derivaret, vicinum inferiorem recipere debere.
pairs.derivation: The full factual setup is kept verbatim and contiguous so 'id suo iure facere' has a referent; the framing 'quaesitum est' was dropped and its interrogative 'an possit id suo iure facere nec ne' normalized to end the question. Answer follows 'respondi' (dropped), kept as the single answering sentence.

pairs.question: Qui duo praedia habebat, in unius venditione aquam, quae in fundo nascebatur, et circa eam aquam late decem pedes exceperat: utrum dominium loci ad eum pertineat an ut per eum locum accedere possit?
pairs.answer: Si ita recepisset: circa eam aquam late pedes decem, iter dumtaxat videri venditoris esse.
pairs.derivation: Setup kept verbatim so the alternatives ('dominium loci' / 'accedere') are intelligible; framing 'quaesitum est' dropped and the double interrogative 'utrum... an...' normalized to end the question. Answer follows 'respondit' (dropped); the editorial quotation marks around 'circa eam aquam late pedes decem' were normalized away, words kept verbatim.

pairs.question: Tria praedia continua trium dominorum adiecta erant: imi praedii dominus ex summo fundo imo fundo servitutem aquae quaesierat et per medium fundum domino concedente in suum agrum ducebat: postea idem summum fundum emit: deinde imum fundum, in quem aquam induxerat, vendidit. Num imus fundus id ius aquae amisisset, quia, cum utraque praedia eiusdem domini facta essent, ipsa sibi servire non potuissent?
pairs.answer: Negavit amisisse servitutem, quia praedium, per quod aqua ducebatur, alterius fuisset.
pairs.derivation: The factual narrative is kept verbatim so 'imus fundus' and 'id ius aquae' have referents; framing 'quaesitum est' was dropped and the 'num... amisisset' interrogative kept. Answer cut at the first full stop after the first 'quia' clause ('alterius fuisset'); what follows ('et quemadmodum servitus...') is the extended reasoning.

pairs.question: Proprium solum vendendo an servitutem talem iniungere possim, ut mihi et vicino serviat? similiter si commune solum vendo, ut mihi et socio serviat, an consequi possim?
pairs.answer: Servitutem recipere nisi sibi nemo potest: adiectio itaque vicini pro supervacuo habenda est, ita ut tota servitus ad eum, qui receperit, pertineat.
pairs.derivation: Two genuine direct interrogatives quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question. Answer follows 'respondi:' (dropped); kept through the colon-joined operative answer ('...pertineat'), stopping before the next sentence ('solum autem communem vendendo...') which addresses the second sub-question separately.

pairs.question: Egi ius illi non esse tigna in parietem meum immissa habere: an et de futuris non immittendis cavendum est?
pairs.answer: Iudicis officio contineri puto, ut de futuro quoque opere caveri debeat.
pairs.derivation: The first clause ('Egi ius illi non esse...') is kept verbatim as setup so 'de futuris non immittendis' has a referent; the interrogative is 'an et de futuris non immittendis cavendum est'. Answer follows 'respondi:' (dropped), kept whole.

pairs.question: Si a te emero, ut mihi liceat ex aedibus meis in aedes tuas stillicidium immittere et postea te sciente ex causa emptionis immissum habeam, an ex hac causa actione quadam vel exceptione tuendus sim?
pairs.derivation: Conditional setup kept verbatim so 'ex hac causa' has a referent; framing 'quaero' dropped and the 'an... tuendus sim' interrogative kept. Answer follows 'respondi' (dropped), kept whole.

pairs.question: Secundum cuius parietem vicinus sterculinum fecerat, ex quo paries madescebat, quemadmodum posset vicinum cogere, ut sterculinum tolleret?
pairs.answer: Si in loco publico id fecisset, per interdictum cogi posse, sed si in privato, de servitute agere oportere.
pairs.derivation: Setup kept verbatim so 'vicinum cogere ut sterculinum tolleret' is intelligible; framing 'consulebatur' dropped and the indirect 'quemadmodum posset...' rendered as the interrogative. Answer follows 'respondi' (dropped); cut at the first full stop after 'agere oportere', before the further clause about 'damni infecti stipulatus esset'.

pairs.question: Is, cuius familia vicinum prohibebat aquam ducere, sui potestatem non faciebat, ne secum agi posset: quid sibi faciendum esset?
pairs.answer: Oportere praetorem causa cognita iubere bona adversarii possideri et non ante inde discedere, quam is actori ius aquae ducendae constituisset.
pairs.derivation: Setup kept verbatim so the plaintiff's predicament is intelligible; framing 'quaerit actor' dropped and 'quid sibi faciendum esset' kept as the interrogative. Answer follows 'respondi' (dropped); cut at the first full stop ('...constituisset'), before the further 'et si quid... siccitatibus detrimenti cepisset' clause.

pairs.question: Testatrix fundo, quem legaverat, casas iunctas habuit: si hae fundo legato non cederent eumque legatarius vindicasset, an iste fundus aliquam servitutem casis deberet aut, si ex fideicommissi causa cum sibi dari legatarius desideraret, heredes servitutem aliquam casis excipere deberent?
pairs.derivation: Setup kept verbatim so 'iste fundus' and 'casis' have referents; framing 'quaesitum est' dropped and the 'an... deberet aut... deberent' interrogative kept. Answer follows 'respondit' (dropped); the one-word answer 'deberi' kept.

pairs.question: Si ego via, quae nobis per vicini fundum debebatur, usus fuero, tu autem constituto tempore cessaveris, an ius tuum amiseris? et e contrario, si vicinus, cui via per nostrum fundum debebatur, per meam partem ierit egerit, tuam partem ingressus non fuerit, an partem tuam liberaverit?
pairs.answer: Si divisus est fundus inter socios regionibus, quod ad servitutem attinet, quae ei fundo debebatur, perinde est, atque si ab initio duobus fundis debita sit.
pairs.derivation: The whole posed problem is two contiguous direct interrogatives ('an ius tuum amiseris?' and 'an partem tuam liberaverit?'), quoted verbatim as the question. Answer follows 'celsus respondit:' (dropped); cut at the first full stop ('...debita sit'), before the continuation 'et sibi quisque dominorum usurpat servitutem...'.
